answer: Synchronized pseudonym parties deter Sybil agents by tying registration to simultaneous human presence. At a shared epoch, operators meet at sites in a signed venue atlas, like a city terrace or river wharf, confirm one-person attendance, and co-sign blind tokens for their agents. Because one body cannot attend two venues concurrently, attackers must hire distinct humans per identity. However, wealthy adversaries can still bypass this limit by paying uninvolved human proxies to attend.
